name: Null Sermon

detectability.signature: Absence of electromagnetic radiation; signal termination boundary; detectable only by the sudden loss of all EM signals at the boundary

proximity: Communications range progressively shortens as the boundary approaches
Sensor sensitivity degrades—distant objects become invisible to instruments
Background cosmic radiation drops to zero, creating an eerie silence on all frequencies
contact: All electromagnetic radiation ceases to propagate—total communications blackout
Sensors, radar, lidar, and all EM-based systems become nonfunctional
Ship lighting functions normally but light does not propagate beyond a few hundred meters
prolonged_exposure: Navigation entirely dependent on inertial systems with no external reference
Crew psychological distress from complete sensory deprivation beyond the ship
Inability to detect obstacles, other vessels, or hazards until physical contact

phenomena: Electromagnetic interference patterns at the boundary—a hard transition from normal to zero
Power systems functioning normally despite EM suppression—the field affects propagation, not generation
Sensor ghosts at the boundary as signals reflect off the field's inner surface
Hull ionization absent despite proximity to stars—no ambient radiation penetrates
hazards: Navigation system failure from loss of all external EM reference
Collision risk—unable to detect obstacles or other vessels
Life support compromise if solar-powered systems lose input
opportunities: Hidden base location—nothing inside is detectable from outside on any EM frequency
Unique research opportunity for understanding EM propagation mechanics
Natural defensive position—guided weapons using EM tracking fail completely
known_incidents: A trade convoy of twelve ships entered Null Sermon accidentally in 2564 when navigation errors compounded during a course correction; the ships spent 19 days navigating blind on inertial guidance alone before emerging, having lost two vessels to collision with each other in the silence.

Intelligence agencies from at least three factions have established covert facilities within Null Sermon, each aware of the others' presence only through the occasional accidental physical encounter in the dark.
description: Null Sermon is silence made manifest. It occupies a sphere 0.7 AU in radius where electromagnetic radiation simply will not propagate. Light, radio, X-rays, gamma rays—none of it passes through. From outside, the field is almost undetectable; it produces no signature of its own, only an absence where signals end. Ships approaching the boundary experience progressive signal degradation, like a radio fading into static, until at the transition point everything stops. Inside, a ship's lights still work, its reactors still generate power, but that light travels only a few hundred meters before the field absorbs it. Beyond the ship's immediate vicinity, there is nothing. Absolute, perfect, electromagnetic nothingness.

Operating within Null Sermon is an exercise in blindness. All sensor systems that rely on electromagnetic radiation—which is to say, nearly all sensor systems—cease to function. Ships navigate by inertial guidance alone, plotting their position mathematically from their last known coordinates and velocity. There is no way to detect obstacles, other vessels, or the boundary itself except by physical contact. Communication between ships requires physical cable connections or crude mechanical signaling. The 2564 convoy disaster demonstrated the consequences: twelve ships entered together and emerged as ten, two having collided in the silent dark with no way to see each other coming.

The origin of Null Sermon is one of the more vexing puzzles in anomaly research. The field does not destroy electromagnetic radiation—it prevents its propagation through a mechanism no theory adequately explains. Energy is conserved; photons emitted within the field are absorbed at extremely short range, their energy converted to heat so efficiently that the interior maintains a slightly elevated temperature. Why this happens, and what maintains the boundary, remains unknown. The field's age cannot be determined because it leaves no traces and contains no datable material. It may have existed since the formation of the universe or appeared yesterday.

Null Sermon's practical value lies in its perfect opacity. Multiple intelligence agencies have built facilities within the field, hidden from any EM-based detection. The irony is that they operate in such complete isolation that they can barely function—resupply requires physical navigation through the dark, and communication with the outside requires courier ships. The facilities exist in a state of mutual unawareness, occasionally discovering each other through accidental physical proximity in a space that admits no other form of contact. For those with reasons to hide, Null Sermon is the ultimate refuge. For everyone else, it is a navigational hazard marked by buoys at its boundary—buoys whose signals simply stop where the silence begins.
